chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Sukeyn, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who says, 'Allah preferred so-and-so (over me).' He said: 'That is abhorred.' It was said, 'What if he says, 'So-and-so has been generous with himself'?' He said: 'There is no problem. Do you not see him opening his mouth at the time of his death two or three times? That is when he is generous with it, because of what he sees of the rewards of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and he used to be niggardly with this.'

key_terms.اسْتَأْثَرَ: To prefer or single out (someone) for a blessing
key_terms.يَجُودُ بِنَفْسِهِ: To be generous with oneself (spending wealth/life)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between abhorred and permissible expressions of 'Allah preferred so-and-so' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the phrase 'Allah preferred so-and-so' is generally disliked (makruh) when implying envy or questioning divine wisdom, yet permissible when referring to the deceased's generosity in spending their wealth. He supports this by noting that the deceased opens their mouth at death, signifying satisfaction with the reward they see, which validates the attribution of preference to their charitable nature. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on intention (niyyah) and the physical signs of spiritual state at the moment of death.
